Democrats flipped nine red Senate seats in this year's historic midterm
elections, and they're
[expected](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results) to
end up with 259 House seats, the largest majority in decades.

The blue tsunami delivered significant wins for progressives, including Abdul
El-Sayed, Troy Jackson, and Peggy Flanagan in the Senate. On the House side,
there were almost too many wins to count.

The left was always going to [expand its
ranks](https://zeteo.com/p/progressives-leftists-heading-to-congress) in the
next Congress. But not every winner has received the attention they deserve.
Here are seven progressive and populist candidates who flipped Republican-held
seats and deserve a closer look.
